title: NY State Assembly · District 64
area: Staten Island's East Shore and part of southern Brooklyn (Bay Ridge), including St. George, Tompkinsville, Grasmere and Grymes Hill.

context.text: Both parties' primaries were canceled. Incumbent Michael Tannousis advanced from the Republican and Conservative Party primaries unopposed; Shpetim Qorraj advanced from the Democratic primary unopposed.

summary.text: Michael Tannousis is the Republican and Conservative Party incumbent seeking a fourth term. A former Bronx and Richmond County assistant district attorney, he has focused his tenure on public safety, bail-reform rollback and opposition to congestion pricing.

background.text: Lives in New York, New York (Staten Island); graduated from Monsignor Farrell High School, earned an undergraduate degree from SUNY Binghamton and a J.D. from Pace Law School.

Began public-service career in 2006 as an aide to then-Minority Leader James Oddo; later worked as an Assistant District Attorney in the Bronx DA's office starting in 2011, then in the Richmond County DA's office from 2016, prosecuting felony violent-crime and narcotics cases.
Son of Greek immigrants displaced by armed conflict in Cyprus.
Assigned in 2025-2026 to the Cities, Codes, Governmental Employees and Judiciary committees.

priorities.text: Stand up for Republican and Conservative values in Albany.
Roll back criminal-justice policies from Albany that he opposes, including bail reform.
Improve quality of life in Staten Island and Brooklyn.
Bring his prosecutorial experience to Albany to support law enforcement.
Create conditions for small businesses to thrive.

positions.summary: Sponsored legislation to repeal congestion pricing in Manhattan.

record.text: Prime-sponsored A06680, which would repeal congestion pricing, restructure MTA board appointments to include one member per NYC borough, and require an independent forensic audit of the MTA; held for consideration in the Corporations, Authorities and Commissions Committee 17-8 on May 28, 2025.
Prime-sponsored A09346 (with Pirozzolo as a co-sponsor), which would incorporate a separate City of Staten Island with its own charter; referred to the Cities Committee.

Prime-sponsored A06358, which would restore judicial discretion in bail decisions and require risk-and-needs assessments for felony defendants; as a member of the Codes Committee, voted no on the committee's 16-6 vote to hold his own bill for consideration (rather than advance it) on May 13, 2025.

Prime-sponsored A06996, which would prohibit siting and construction of battery energy storage systems in Assembly District 64; held for consideration in the Local Governments Committee 14-6 on May 18, 2026.

candidates.name: Shpetim Qorraj

summary.text: Shpetim Qorraj, also known as Tim Qorraj, is the Democratic nominee challenging incumbent Michael Tannousis. He is a Staten Island small-business owner who has not previously held elected office.

background.text: Born in Kosovo, lost his father, a veteran, at age 13 during the war there; came to the United States in 2011 and now lives in the South Beach neighborhood of Staten Island.
Holds a Master's degree in Criminal Law.
Owner of Skyler Services Group LLC, a Staten Island business providing renovation, porter, super and maintenance services.

priorities.text: Address New York's affordability crisis, including housing costs, small-business regulatory burdens, and the cost of utilities, food and other essentials.

Secure state funding for Staten Island transportation, including keeping the Verrazzano Bridge resident toll discount, reducing congestion on Hylan Blvd, and creating a fast-ferry dock in Great Kills.
Support public education funding and after-school programming, and push for construction of the East Shore seawall promised after Hurricane Sandy.

positions.summary: Supports hiring more police officers for the local precinct and enhancing retirement benefits to attract recruits.
positions.quote: Support increasing hiring of police officers to be assigned to the 122 Precinct and expand the Community Affairs department to have more officers on call to address quality of life issues.

candidates.researchNotes: No completed Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey or independent news coverage was found for Qorraj, but his campaign website (linked from his Ballotpedia infobox) has an about page and issues page that were used for background and priorities.

sources.title: Mike Tannousis: 5 Reasons Why I'm Running

researchNotes: Tannousis's 'issues' page returned a 404, so his priorities are drawn from his 'Meet Mike' bio and a 2019 'Reasons I'm Running' post (both still linked from his active 2026 campaign site). Qorraj's Ballotpedia infobox links a campaign website (timforassembly.com, under the name 'Tim Qorraj'), which supplied his background, priorities and one position; no completed Candidate Connection survey or independent news coverage was found for him.
